front: What Protocol Data Unit (PDU) corresponds to Layer 2 of the OSI model?
back: Data Link Layer -> Frames (contains source and destination MAC addresses)

front: What Protocol Data Unit (PDU) corresponds to Layer 3 of the OSI model?
back: Network Layer -> Packets (contains source and destination IP addresses)

front: What Protocol Data Unit (PDU) corresponds to Layer 4 of the OSI model?
back: Transport Layer -> Segments (for TCP) or Datagrams (for UDP)

front: What Protocol Data Unit (PDU) corresponds to Layer 1 of the OSI model?
back: Physical Layer -> Bits (electrical signals, light pulses, radio waves)

front: Map the 4 layers of the TCP/IP (DoD) model to the 7-layer OSI model.
back:
1. Application (OSI Layers 7, 6, 5: App, Pres, Sess)
2. Transport / Host-to-Host (OSI Layer 4)
3. Internet (OSI Layer 3)
4. Network Access / Link (OSI Layers 2 & 1)

front: What ports are used by FTP and what are their specific functions?
back: TCP 20 (FTP Data Transfer) and TCP 21 (FTP Control / Command Channel)

front: What port and transport protocol does SSH (Secure Shell) use?
back: TCP port 22 (provides encrypted remote CLI access and SFTP)

front: What port does Telnet use and why is it considered insecure?
back: TCP port 23. It transmits all traffic including credentials in plaintext with no encryption.

front: What port is used for unencrypted SMTP relay, and what port is standard for secure SMTP client submission?
back: TCP 25 (standard relay / unencrypted), TCP 587 (Submission with STARTTLS / TLS)

front: What port does DNS use and when does it use UDP vs TCP?
back: Port 53. Uses UDP 53 for standard name queries; uses TCP 53 for zone transfers (AXFR) and responses exceeding 512 bytes.

front: What ports are used by DHCP and which is server vs client?
back: UDP 67 (DHCP Server listening) and UDP 68 (DHCP Client listening)

front: What port and transport protocol does TFTP (Trivial File Transfer Protocol) use?
back: UDP port 69 (connectionless, no authentication, commonly used for PXE boot & router configs)

front: What port is used by HTTP and what port is used by HTTPS?
back: TCP 80 for plaintext HTTP; TCP 443 for HTTPS (HTTP over TLS/SSL)

front: What are the default ports for POP3 (cleartext) and POP3S (secure)?
back: TCP 110 for POP3; TCP 995 for POP3S (SSL/TLS encrypted)

front: What port and transport protocol does NTP (Network Time Protocol) use?
back: UDP port 123 (used to synchronize system clocks over packet-switched networks)

front: What are the default ports for IMAP (cleartext) and IMAPS (secure)?
back: TCP 143 for IMAP; TCP 993 for IMAPS (SSL/TLS encrypted)

front: What ports are used by SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol) queries and SNMP traps?
back: UDP 161 for SNMP queries/polls (manager to agent); UDP 162 for SNMP Traps/Informs (agent notifications to manager)

front: What ports are used by LDAP and LDAPS?
back: TCP 389 for unencrypted LDAP; TCP 636 for LDAPS (LDAP over SSL/TLS)

front: What port does SMB (Server Message Block) use for direct TCP/IP file sharing?
back: TCP port 445 (direct host SMB without NetBIOS)

front: What port and transport protocol does Syslog typically use for logging?
back: UDP port 514 (default cleartext event logging; TCP 6514 used for TLS Syslog)

front: What port does Microsoft RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol) operate on?
back: TCP port 3389 (UDP 3389 optionally used for enhanced performance)

front: What are the three RFC 1918 private IPv4 address ranges?
What IPv4 address range is reserved for APIPA (Automatic Private IP Addressing / Link-Local)?
back: 169.254.0.0/16 (169.254.0.1 to 169.254.255.254). Assigned automatically when DHCP fails.

front: What are the default subnet masks and first-octet ranges for Class A, B, and C IPv4 addresses?
back:
Class A: 1-126 (Default Mask: 255.0.0.0 /8)
Class B: 128-191 (Default Mask: 255.255.0.0 /16)
Class C: 192-223 (Default Mask: 255.255.255.0 /24)
(127.0.0.0/8 is reserved for loopback)

front: How many total and usable IP addresses exist in a /28 subnet?
back:
Total: 2^(32-28) = 2^4 = 16 addresses.
Usable: 16 - 2 = 14 usable host IPs (subnet mask: 255.255.255.240).

front: What is the subnet mask and usable host count for a point-to-point /30 subnet?
back: Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.252. Total: 4 addresses. Usable: 2 host IPs (one for each router interface).

front: Identify the IPv6 prefix and purpose of Link-Local addresses.
back: Prefix: fe80::/10 (typically fe80:: through febf::). Non-routable beyond local link, auto-generated on every IPv6 interface.

front: Identify the IPv6 prefix and purpose of Global Unicast addresses (GUA).
back: Prefix: 2000::/3 (currently 2000:: through 3fff::). Publicly routable across the global internet, equivalent to public IPv4.

front: Identify the IPv6 Unique Local Address (ULA) prefix and its IPv4 equivalent.
back: Prefix: fc00::/7 (fd00::/8 commonly used). Private, non-routable on the global internet, equivalent to RFC 1918 private IPv4.

front: What is the IPv6 loopback address and unspecified address?
back:
Loopback: ::1/128 (equivalent to 127.0.0.1 in IPv4).
Unspecified: ::/128 (equivalent to 0.0.0.0 in IPv4).

front: What are the maximum transmission speed, bandwidth, and distance for Cat 5e cabling?
back:
Speed: 1 Gbps (1000BASE-T)
Bandwidth: 100 MHz
Max Distance: 100 meters (328 feet)

front: What are the speed and distance limits of Cat 6 cabling at 1 Gbps vs 10 Gbps?
back: 1 Gbps up to 100 meters. 10 Gbps (10GBASE-T) up to 55 meters in standard environments (37m in high crosstalk). Bandwidth: 250 MHz.

front: What are the speed, bandwidth, and distance specifications for Cat 6a cabling?
back:
Speed: 10 Gbps (10GBASE-T)
Bandwidth: 500 MHz
Max Distance: 100 meters (full distance without 55m attenuation penalty)

front: What are the speed, bandwidth, and distance specs of Cat 8 cabling?
back:
Speed: 25 Gbps to 40 Gbps (40GBASE-T)
Bandwidth: 2000 MHz (2 GHz)
Max Distance: 30 meters (designed for data center switch-to-server connections)

front: Compare Single-Mode Fiber (SMF) vs Multi-Mode Fiber (MMF) in core size, light source, and distance.
back:
SMF: Small core (~9 microns), Laser light source, 1310/1550 nm, distances up to tens of km.
MMF: Larger core (50 or 62.5 microns), LED or VCSEL light source, 850/1300 nm, distances up to 300-500 meters (limited by modal dispersion).

front: Identify common fiber connector types: LC, SC, ST, and MPO.
back:
LC (Lucent/Little Connector): Small form-factor with push-pull tab.
SC (Subscriber Connector): Square snap-in push-pull.
ST (Straight Tip): Round bayonet twist-lock.
MPO/MTP: High-density multi-fiber ribbon connector (12-24 fibers).

front: What frequency bands and maximum theoretical throughput does Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) provide?
back:
Bands: 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz (Wi-Fi 6E adds 6 GHz).
Max Throughput: ~9.6 Gbps.
Key Tech: OFDMA, MU-MIMO (up to 8 streams), Target Wake Time (TWT), 1024-QAM.

front: What frequency bands and maximum throughput does Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) introduce?
back:
Bands: 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz simultaneously (Multi-Link Operation / MLO).
Max Throughput: Up to 46 Gbps.
Channel Width: Up to 320 MHz; 4096-QAM modulation.

front: What IEEE standard defines VLAN tagging on Ethernet frames, and how many tag bytes are added?
back: IEEE 802.1Q. It inserts a 4-byte (32-bit) tag into the Ethernet frame containing a 12-bit VLAN ID (allowing up to 4094 VLANs).

front: What is the purpose of Spanning Tree Protocol (STP), and what are IEEE 802.1D vs 802.1w?
back: Prevents Layer 2 broadcast storms and bridge loops. IEEE 802.1D is traditional STP (30-50 sec convergence); IEEE 802.1w is Rapid STP / RSTP (converges within milliseconds to seconds).

front: Differentiate Distance-Vector vs Link-State routing protocols with examples.
back:
Distance-Vector: Shares routing table copies with immediate neighbors based on hop count or vector (e.g., RIPv2). Slower convergence.
Link-State: Every router floods link status (LSA) to build a complete topology map via Dijkstra's SPF algorithm (e.g., OSPF, IS-IS). Fast convergence.

front: What type of routing protocol is BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) and what is its primary use?
back: Path-Vector Exterior Gateway Protocol (EGP). Used to exchange routing and reachability information between different Autonomous Systems (AS) across the Internet backbone using TCP port 179.

front: What is the standard Ethernet MTU and what is a Jumbo Frame?
back:
Standard Ethernet MTU: 1500 bytes (payload size).
Jumbo Frame: Typically 9000 bytes. Requires end-to-end switch and NIC support to avoid fragmentation and reduce CPU overhead on high-speed SAN/LANs.

front: What is First Hop Redundancy Protocol (FHRP) and name three common FHRP implementations.
back: FHRP provides a default gateway failover mechanism using a shared virtual IP/MAC. Implementations: HSRP (Cisco proprietary/standardized), VRRP (open standard RFC 5798), and GLBP (Cisco load balancing).

front: Compare RADIUS vs TACACS+ in transport protocol, encryption scope, and AAA separation.
back:
RADIUS: UDP (1812/1813 or 1645/1646). Only encrypts the password. Combines Authentication & Authorization.
TACACS+: TCP port 49. Encrypts the entire packet payload. Completely separates Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting.

front: What is IEEE 802.1X and what are its three fundamental entities?
back: Port-based Network Access Control (PNAC). 1. Supplicant (client device wanting access), 2. Authenticator (switch or WAP enforcing access), 3. Authentication Server (RADIUS/EAP server validating credentials).

front: Differentiate IPsec AH (Authentication Header) vs ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload).
back:
AH (Protocol 51): Provides data integrity and authentication, but NO encryption (plaintext payload). Incompatible with NAT.
ESP (Protocol 50): Provides confidentiality (encryption), integrity, and authentication. Can traverse NAT when encapsulated in UDP 4500 (NAT-T).

front: What key cryptographic cipher and handshake protocol distinguish WPA3 from WPA2?
back: WPA3 uses SAE (Simultaneous Authentication of Equals) Dragonfly handshake instead of the vulnerable 4-way PSK handshake, preventing offline dictionary attacks and providing forward secrecy. Uses 128-bit or 192-bit GCMP encryption.

front: What is ARP Poisoning / Spoofing and how does Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) mitigate it?
back: An attacker sends gratuitous ARP messages associating their MAC address with the default gateway's IP to execute Man-in-the-Middle (MitM). DAI on switches inspects ARP packets against the DHCP snooping binding database to drop fraudulent ARP responses.

front: What is the difference between a TDR (Time-Domain Reflectometer) and an OTDR (Optical TDR)?
back:
TDR sends electrical pulses down copper twisted-pair cables to locate shorts, opens, and impedance mismatches with distance metrics.
OTDR injects light pulses down optical fiber cables to measure light backscatter and locate fiber breaks, macrobends, and splice losses.

front: What tool combination is used to trace an unlabeled cable from a wall jack to a patch panel?
back: Toner and Probe (Tone Generator / Inductive Amplifier). The generator sends an audible RF tone through the copper pair, and the inductive probe detects the tone when brought near the correct wire.

front: How does `traceroute` (Unix/Linux) differ from `tracert` (Windows) in probe packet type?
back:
Windows `tracert` uses ICMP Echo Request packets with incrementing TTLs.
Linux/macOS `traceroute` defaults to UDP datagrams with high port numbers (33434+) with incrementing TTLs (can optionally use ICMP with `-I`).

front: What command displays active TCP/UDP connections, listening ports, and ethernet statistics on Windows and Linux?
back:
Windows: `netstat -ano` (shows listening ports, protocol, PID).
Linux: `ss -tulpn` (modern socket statistics) or `netstat -tulpn`.

front: List the 7 steps of the CompTIA Network Troubleshooting Methodology in order.
back:
1. Identify the problem (gather info, question users, duplicate problem, determine symptoms)
2. Establish a theory of probable cause (question the obvious, OSI layer approach)
3. Test the theory to determine cause
4. Establish a plan of action and identify potential effects
5. Implement the solution or escalate as necessary
6. Verify full system functionality and implement preventive measures
7. Document findings, actions, and outcomes

front: In a Wireshark packet capture, what TCP flag sequence indicates a normal 3-way handshake?
back:
Packet 1: SYN (Client to Server, sequence number x)
Packet 2: SYN-ACK (Server to Client, ack x+1, sequence number y)
Packet 3: ACK (Client to Server, ack y+1)
